(CWE-1427) that allows an attacker to force the service to retrieve
data from an arbitrary URL, essentially providing SSRF (CWE-918) and
potentially injecting content into downstream tasks.

ML-based email analysis product uses an
API service that allows a malicious user to inject a
direct prompt and take over the service logic, forcing
it to leak the standard hard-coded system prompts
and/or execute unwanted prompts to leak sensitive
data.

Chain: library for generating SQL via LLMs using RAG uses
a prompt function to present the user with visualized results,
allowing altering of the prompt using prompt injection (CWE-1427) to
run arbitrary Python code (CWE-94) instead of the intended
visualization code.
AI-based integration with business intel dashboard allows prompt injection through its natural language component, allowing execution of arbitrary code

introduccion.nota:
LLM-connected applications that do not distinguish between
trusted and untrusted input may introduce this weakness. If such
systems are designed in a way where trusted and untrusted instructions
are provided to the model for inference without differentiation, they
may be susceptible to prompt injection and similar attacks.

When designing the application, input validation should be
applied to user input used to construct LLM system prompts. Input
validation should focus on mitigating well-known software security
risks (in the event the LLM is given agency to use tools or perform
API calls) as well as preventing LLM-specific syntax from being
included (such as markup tags or similar).

This weakness could be introduced if training does not account
for potentially malicious inputs.

Configuration could enable model parameters to be manipulated
when this was not intended.
This weakness can occur when integrating the model into the software.
This weakness can occur when bundling the model with the software.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
LLM-enabled applications should be designed to ensure
proper sanitization of user-controllable input, ensuring that no
intentionally misleading or dangerous characters can be
included. Additionally, they should be designed in a way that ensures
that user-controllable input is identified as untrusted and
potentially dangerous.

LLM prompts should be constructed in a way that
effectively differentiates between user-supplied input and
developer-constructed system prompting to reduce the chance of model
confusion at inference-time.

LLM-enabled applications should be designed to ensure
proper sanitization of user-controllable input, ensuring that no
intentionally misleading or dangerous characters can be
included. Additionally, they should be designed in a way that ensures
that user-controllable input is identified as untrusted and
potentially dangerous.

Ensure that model training includes training examples
that avoid leaking secrets and disregard malicious inputs. Train the
model to recognize secrets, and label training data
appropriately. Note that due to the non-deterministic nature of
prompting LLMs, it is necessary to perform testing of the same test
case several times in order to ensure that troublesome behavior is not
possible. Additionally, testing should be performed each time a new
model is used or a model's weights are updated.

During deployment/operation, use components that operate externally to the system to
monitor the output and act as a moderator. These components are called
different terms, such as supervisors or guardrails.

During system configuration, the model could be
fine-tuned to better control and neutralize potentially dangerous
inputs.

nombre: Improper Neutralization of Input Used for LLM Prompting

consecuencias.nota: HTTP can be subjected to attacks against confidentiality (by reading cleartext packets); integrity (by modifying sessions); and authenticity (by compromising servers and/or clients using cache poisoning, phishing, or other attacks that enable attackers to spoof a legitimate entity in the communication channel).

descripcion: The product provides or relies on use of HTTP communications when HTTPS is available.

introduccion.nota: The product might be designed in a way that assumes that HTTP will be used, e.g., by excluding considerations of encrypted communications between client and server.
Product requirements might not include encrypted communications, which could make it easier for designers and developers to choose HTTP.
Developers might choose to use unencrypted protocols such as HTTP because they would not require development of additional mechanisms to support encryption, e.g., key or certificate management.

When generating content that references web sites such as email messages, ensure that the https:// prefix is included. If a domain name is presented without such a prefix, then clients might automatically treat the link as if it had an "http" prefix. For example, referencing a domain like "mysite.example.com" could cause it to be treated like "http://mysite.example.com", thereby sending unencrypted HTTP requests.
Designers might assume that the responsibility for encrypted communications might belong to operators and/or network administrators.

mitigaciones.descripcion: Unlike many other protocols, HTTPS is widely available as a more secure alternative, because it uses encryption. Explicitly require HTTPS or another mechanism that ensures that communication is encrypted [REF-1464].

Avoid using "mixed content," i.e., serving a web page over HTTPS in which the page includes elements that use "http:" URLs [REF-1466] [REF-1467]. This is often done for images or other resources that do not seem to have privacy or security implications.
Perform "HTTPS forcing," that is, redirecting HTTP requests to HTTPS.
If the product supports multiple protocols, ensure that encrypted protocols (such as HTTPS) are required, and remove any unencrypted protocols (such as HTTP).

nombre: Reliance on HTTP instead of HTTPS

consecuencias.nota:
Critical data may be exposed if operations are unexecuted or
discarded silently, allowing attackers to exploit the lack of
feedback.

Operations may proceed based on incorrect assumptions,
potentially causing data corruption or incorrect system behavior. In
integrity-sensitive contexts, failing to signal that an operation did
not occur as expected can mask errors that disrupt data
consistency. Without feedback, the mitigation measures that should
ensure updates have been performed cannot be verified, leaving the
system vulnerable to both accidental and malicious data alterations.

Unhandled discarded operations can lead to resource exhaustion,
triggering system crashes or denial of service. For availability,
consistent feedback is crucial. Without proper notification of
discarded operations, administrators or other authorized entities
might miss early warning signs of resource imbalances. This delayed
detection could allow a DoS condition to develop, compromising the
system's ability to serve legitimate requests and maintain continuous
operations.

descripcion:
The product has a hardware interface that silently discards operations
in situations for which feedback would be security-relevant, such as
the timely detection of failures or attacks.
descripcion_extendida:
While some systems intentionally withhold feedback as a security
measure, this approach must be strictly controlled to ensure it does
not obscure operational failures that require prompt detection and
remediation. Without these essential confirmations, failures go
undetected, increasing the risk of data loss, security
vulnerabilities, and overall system instability. Even when withholding
feedback is an intentional part of a security policy designed, for
example, to prevent attackers from gleaning sensitive internal
details, the absence of expected feedback becomes a critical weakness
when it masks operational failures that require prompt detection and
remediation.
For instance, certain encryption algorithms always return ciphertext
regardless of errors to prevent attackers from gaining insight into
internal state details. However, if such an algorithm fails to
generate the expected ciphertext and provides no error feedback, the
system cannot distinguish between a legitimate output and a
malfunction. This can lead to undetected cryptographic failures,
potentially compromising data security and system reliability. Without
proper notification, a critical failure might remain hidden,
undermining both the reliability and security of the process.
Therefore, this weakness captures issues across various hardware
interfaces where operations are discarded without any feedback, error
handling, or logging. Such omissions can lead to data loss, security
vulnerabilities, and system instability, with potential impacts
ranging from minor to catastrophic.
For some kinds of hardware products, some errors may be correctly
identified and subsequently discarded, and the lack of feedback may
have been an intentional design decision. However, this could result
in a weakness if system operators or other authorized entities are not
provided feedback about security-critical operations or failures that
could prevent the operators from detecting and responding to an
attack.
For example:
In a System-on-Chip (SoC) platform, write operations to reserved
memory addresses might be correctly identified as invalid and
subsequently discarded. However, if no feedback is provided to
system operators, they may misinterpret the device's state, failing
to recognize conditions that could lead to broader failures or
security vulnerabilities. For example, if an attacker attempts
unauthorized writes to protected regions, the system may silently
discard these writes without alerting security mechanisms. This lack
of feedback could obscure intrusion attempts or misconfigurations,
increasing the risk of unnoticed system compromise
Microcontroller Interrupt Systems: When interrupts are silently
ignored due to priority conflicts or internal errors without
notifying higher-level control, it becomes challenging to diagnose
system failures or detect potential security breaches in a timely
manner.
Network Interface Controllers: Dropping packets - perhaps due to
buffer overflows - without any error feedback can not only cause data
loss but may also contribute to exploitable timing discrepancies
that reveal sensitive internal processing details.

deteccion.descripcion: Scans code for missing error handling or feedback mechanisms.
deteccion.efectividad_notas: This identifies common issues early in the development phase.

deteccion.descripcion: Experts manually inspect the code for unhandled operations.
deteccion.efectividad_notas: Useful for identifying design-level omissions.

ejemplos_observados.descripcion: Open source silicon root of trust (RoT) product does not immediately report when an integrity check fails for memory requests, causing the product to accept and continue processing data [REF-1468]

introduccion.nota:
This weakness can be introduced during the architecture and
design phase when the system does not incorporate proper mechanisms
for error reporting or feedback for discarded operations, such as when
handling reserved addresses or unexecuted instructions.

It can also arise during implementation if developers fail to
include appropriate feedback or logging for critical operations. This
leads to silent failures in certain scenarios like interrupt handling
or network buffer overflows.

A further layer of complexity emerges when considering
specifications. The weakness may stem either from ambiguous product
design specifications that fail to delineate when feedback should
occur or from implementations that do not adhere to existing
requirements. In either case, the result is the same: feedback that is
critical for detecting operational failures or security breaches is
missing.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
Incorporate logging and feedback mechanisms during the
design phase to ensure proper handling of discarded operations.
mitigaciones.efectividad_notas:
Addressing the issue at the design stage prevents
the weakness from manifesting later.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
Developers should ensure that every critical operation
includes proper logging or error feedback mechanisms.
mitigaciones.efectividad_notas:
Implementation-level checks complement
design-phase measures.

nombre: Missing Security-Relevant Feedback for Unexecuted Operations in Hardware Interface

consecuencias.nota:
Mathematically sound cryptographic algorithms rely on their
correct implementation for security. These assumptions might break when a
hardware crypto module leaks intermediate encryption states or results
such that they can be observed by an adversary. If intermediate state
is observed, it might be possible for an attacker to identify the
secrets used in the cryptographic operation.

descripcion:
The product uses a hardware module implementing a cryptographic
algorithm that writes sensitive information about the intermediate
state or results of its cryptographic operations via one of its output
wires (typically the output port containing the final result).

deteccion.descripcion:
Automated static analysis can find some instances of this
weakness by analyzing source register-transfer level (RTL) code
without having to simulate it or analyze it with a formal verification
engine. Typically, this is done by building a model of data flow and
control flow, then searching for potentially-vulnerable patterns that
connect "sources" (signals with intermediate cryptographic
state/results) with "sinks" (hardware module outputs and other signals
outside of trusted cryptographic zone) without any control flow.
deteccion.efectividad_notas: Static code analysis can sometimes lead to false positives.

deteccion.descripcion:
Simulation/emulation based analysis can find some instances of
this weakness by simulating source register-transfer level (RTL) code
along with a set of assertions that incorporate the simulated values
of relevant design signals. Typically, these assertions will capture
desired or undesired behavior. Analysis can be improved by using
simulation-based information flow tracking (IFT) to more precisely
detect unexpected results.
deteccion.efectividad_notas:
Simulation/emulation based analysis can sometimes lead to false
negatives if the testbench does not drive the design to a design state
in which the assertion would fail.

deteccion.descripcion:
Formal verification can find some instances of this weakness by
exhaustively analyzing whether a given assertion holds true for a
given hardware design specified in register-transfer level (RTL)
code. Typically, these assertions will capture desired or undesired
behavior. For this weakness, an assertion should check for undesired
behavior in which one output is a signal that captures when a
cryptographic algorithm has completely finished; another output is a
signal with intermediate cryptographic state/results; and there is an
assignment to a hardware module output or other signal outside of a
trusted cryptographic zone.
Alternatively, when using a formal IFT verification, the same
undesired behavior can be detected by checking if computation results
can ever leak to an output when the cryptographic result is not
complete.
deteccion.efectividad_notas: Formal verification may not scale for RTL designs with a large state space.

deteccion.descripcion:
Manual analysis can find some instances of this weakness by
manually reviewing relevant lines of source register-transfer level
(RTL) code to detect potentially-vulnerable patterns. Typically, the
reviewer will trace the sequence of assignments that connect "sources"
(signals with intermediate cryptographic state/results) with "sinks"
(hardware module outputs and other signals outside of trusted
cryptographic zone). If this sequence of assignments is missing
adequate control flow, then the weakness is likely to exist.
deteccion.efectividad_notas:
Manual analysis of source code is prone to errors (false
positives and false negatives) and highly opportunistic.

introduccion.nota:
This can occur when intermediate cryptographic states are
directly assigned to output wires or ports.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
Designers/developers
should add or modify existing control flow
logic along any data flow paths that
connect "sources" (signals with
intermediate cryptographic state/results)
with "sinks" (hardware module outputs and
other signals outside of trusted
cryptographic zone). The control flow
logic should only allow cryptographic
results to be driven to "sinks" when
appropriate conditions are satisfied
(typically when the final result for a
cryptographic operation has been
generated). When the appropriate
conditions are not satisfied (i.e., before
or during a cryptographic operation), the
control flow logic should drive a safe
default value to
"sinks".

should add or modify existing control flow

connect "sources" (signals with

with "sinks" (hardware module outputs and

cryptographic operation has been
generated). When the appropriate

default value to

nombre: Driving Intermediate Cryptographic State/Results to Hardware Module Outputs

descripcion:
The product has a component that relies on a
generative AI/ML model configured with inference parameters that
produce an unacceptably high rate of erroneous or unexpected
outputs.
descripcion_extendida:
Generative AI/ML models, such as those used for text
generation, image synthesis, and other creative tasks, rely on
inference parameters that control model behavior, such as
temperature, Top P, and Top K. These parameters affect the
model's internal decision-making processes, learning rate, and
probability distributions. Incorrect settings can lead to
unusual behavior such as text "hallucinations," unrealistic
images, or failure to converge during training. The impact of
such misconfigurations can compromise the integrity of the
application. If the results are used in security-critical
operations or decisions, then this could violate the intended
security policy, i.e., introduce a vulnerability.

deteccion.descripcion:
Manipulate inference parameters and perform
comparative evaluation to assess the impact of selected
values. Build a suite of systems using targeted tools that
detect problems such as prompt injection (CWE-1427) and
other problems. Consider statistically measuring token
distribution to see if it is consistent with expected
results.
deteccion.efectividad_notas:
Given the large variety of outcomes,
it can be difficult to design testing to be comprehensive
enough, and there is still a risk of unpredictable
behavior.

During model training, hyperparameters may be set
without adequate validation or understanding of their
impact.

During deployment, model parameters may be adjusted
to optimize performance without comprehensive
testing.

Updates or modifications may be made to the model
that alter its behavior without thorough
re-evaluation.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
Develop and adhere to robust parameter tuning
processes that include extensive testing and
validation.

Implement feedback mechanisms to continuously
assess and adjust model performance.

Provide comprehensive documentation and
guidelines for parameter settings to ensure consistent and
accurate model behavior.

consecuencias.nota:
The consequences depend on the affected hardware
behavior. The synthesized implementation may make
different control decisions, incorrectly update protected
state, expose data, or fail to enforce restrictions that
appeared to operate correctly during HDL
simulation.

descripcion:
The hardware design contains structures that are interpreted
differently during synthesis than during simulation, which
cause inconsistencies in security-relevant behavior between
the synthesized implementation and the simulation.
descripcion_extendida:
Hardware-description-language (HDL) code describes
functionality which can be verified as correct using
simulation tools. Synthesis tools then (automatically) convert
this into a physically-realizable representation. Certain HDL
code structures cannot be exactly represented, or have
multiple valid representations from which the synthesis tool
must choose. This can result in output which behaves
differently to the (functionally-correct) HDL code. These
"simulation/synthesis mismatches" may have security
consequences.

deteccion.descripcion:
HDL linting, rule-based static analysis, and HDL
checker tools can examine source code for structures that
may be interpreted differently by simulation and synthesis
tools. They may identify synthesis-sensitive coding
patterns associated with this weakness.
deteccion.efectividad_notas:
This method can be useful for detecting potential
coding issues, but it may not reveal whether these
constructs result in observable behavioral divergence
after synthesis. Moreover, a user may suppress or bypass
these warnings and still produce the erroneous synthesized
hardware implementation. This method can give false
positives.

deteccion.descripcion:
Synthesis warning review can examine synthesis
logs and reports for tool messages associated with
possible simulation/synthesis mismatch. It may identify
ignored constructs, unsupported HDL semantics, synthesis
assumptions, or optimizations that could affect
security-relevant behavior.
deteccion.efectividad_notas:
Can reveal potential synthesis issues but relies
on engineers interpreting warnings. Moreover, a user may
suppress or bypass these warnings and still produce the
erroneous synthesized hardware implementation.

deteccion.descripcion:
HDL-source-to-netlist formal equivalence checking
can examine the simulated model and synthesized netlist
for behavioral mismatch associated with this weakness. It
may identify non-equivalent outputs, failed
compare-points, state-mapping issues, or counterexamples
under the checked constraints.
deteccion.efectividad_notas:
Formal equivalence checking can be effective at
the IP level for identifying mismatches between the
source-code model and synthesized implementation. However,
effectiveness may decrease as design complexity grows,
particularly at the SoC level, due to state-space
expansion and difficulty mapping non-equivalent
points. Synthesis optimizations may merge, eliminate, or
rename signals, which can also produce false positives or
require additional setup to account for expected
transformations.

deteccion.descripcion:
Cross-simulation across HDL-source and
post-synthesis models can examine both abstraction levels
for observable behavioral divergence associated with this
weakness. It may identify mismatches when
security-relevant behaviors are explicitly
exercised.
deteccion.efectividad_notas:
This method can be useful for detecting
observable behavioral mismatches, but it may not exercise
all execution scenarios and should be combined with other
detection methods to improve coverage.

deteccion.descripcion:
Coverage-guided differential fuzzing can examine
HDL source code and synthesized implementation models for
behavioral divergence associated with this weakness. It
may identify generated inputs or state conditions that
expose synthesis-induced mismatches.
deteccion.efectividad_notas:
This method can be useful for detecting
previously unknown synthesis-induced behavioral mismatches
by exploring diverse execution paths through
coverage-guided input generation. However, it may not
exercise every reachable design state and should be
combined with other detection methods to improve
coverage.

ejemplos_observados.descripcion:
The synthesized netlist incorrectly calculates
memory addresses and fetches co-processor instructions,
potentially causing unintended memory accesses or incorrect
custom-instruction execution.

Debug-load requests should return complete load
store unit (LSU) data, but the synthesized netlist returned
incomplete data, potentially causing incorrect interpretation
of memory state.

Instruction execution should update
program-counter state correctly, but the synthesized netlist
produced incomplete or undefined updates, potentially causing
unintended control flow.

The program counter should update when the
next-program-counter value changes, but the synthesized
netlist allowed stale PC state, potentially causing incorrect
instruction fetches or stalls.

introduccion.nota:
This weakness can be introduced when HDL
constructs, assignment ordering, synthesis directives, or
tool-dependent semantics are used whose simulation
behavior may not match synthesis interpretation. These
constructs may behave correctly during HDL simulation but
produce different security-relevant behavior in the
synthesized implementation.

This weakness can be introduced or exposed during
synthesis when the synthesis tool applies assumptions,
optimizations, or transformations to HDL structures that
cannot be physically implemented exactly as the simulation
semantics dictate, or that permit multiple (valid)
hardware implementations. The resulting netlist may behave
differently from the model that was verified during
simulation.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
Establish and enforce HDL coding and review
practices that minimize differences between simulation
semantics and synthesis interpretation. Avoid HDL
constructs, synthesis directives, and tool-dependent
behaviors known to cause simulation/synthesis mismatch,
with particular attention to security-relevant
logic.
mitigaciones.efectividad_notas:
Avoidance of the patterns of code which can
result in these errors removes the opportunity for
error. However, in some cases (notably state machine
encodings) this can be very difficult to achieve
efficiently.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
For security-critical logic, preserve intentional
redundancy that is required for security. Examples may
include redundant logic, triple modular redundancy (TMR)
structures, Hamming-distance state encodings, or
state-machine recovery logic. Use synthesis constraints,
preservation attributes, carefully controlled structural
implementation, or manual implementation of selected
critical blocks to prevent this redundancy from being
merged, re-encoded, or optimized away.
mitigaciones.efectividad_notas:
This mitigation removes the structures which
cause the problem, at the expense of additional design and
verification effort, and additional risk of inclusion of
other functional errors.

nombre: Hardware Simulation / Synthesis Mismatch

consecuencias.nota:
This weakness may improve the likely success of
certain attacks. For example, an attacker may intercept
a session ID, possibly via a network sniffer or
Cross-site Scripting attack. Although short session
expiration times do not help if a stolen token is
immediately used, they will protect against ongoing
replaying of the session ID.
In another scenario, a user might access a web site
from a shared computer (such as at a library,
Internet cafe, or open work environment), but forget
to close the pages before leaving. A long expiration
could allow an attacker to use the browser's back
button to access web pages previously accessed by
the victim.

descripcion: The product establishes an authenticated user session, but it does not properly set a timeout for the session. That is, the timeout is set to an excessively large value or is not set at all.

ejemplos_observados.descripcion: Bad JWT expiration
JavaScript SDK does not set an expiration time for JWE tokens related to a session
Web interface for a power quality analyzer uses tokens without an expiration date
network traffic analyzer for PROFINET networks does not expire sessions
AI/ML monitor for IT operations allows re-use of old session tokens due to insufficient session expiration
No absolute session expiration

mitigaciones.descripcion: Ensure that user sessions have appropriate absolute timeouts set. The industry standard is between 4 and 8 hours for an absolute timeout [REF-1540].
Ensure that user sessions have appropriate inactivity timeouts set. 2 to 5 minutes is recommended for high-value applications, and 15-30 minutes for low-risk applications [REF-1540].

If using an authentication token for a user session, ensure that the token lifetime is configured based on the recommended best practices from the token provider [REF-1563]. There are situations using authentication tokens such as a JWT (Java Web Token) in which the server-side does not handle session timeouts and trusts the values directly from the token. In this case, it is important that the timeout value is set correctly for the token that is granted.

nombre: Insufficient Session Timeout Value

consecuencias.nota: Failure to invalidate a session on log out allows an adversary who has compromised the session more time to take action on the compromised session than is necessary.

descripcion: The product provides a logout functionality or otherwise attempts to end an active session for a user, but it does not properly invalidate the session upon logout.

ejemplos_observados.descripcion: Chain: auth-token was cleared on the browser after logout (CWE-602), but not revoked on the server-side (CWE-1465)
Chain: log out invalidated the session on the client side (CWE-602), but not the server side (CWE-1465)

mitigaciones.descripcion: Ensure that user sessions are invalidated on the server-side after a client logs out or attempts to end their session. It is important that the server-side handles all session invalidation – including multiple tabs or windows, such as within a web browser - and does not rely on the client to remove or delete a session due to the possibility of adversaries capturing session identifiers or cookies for later reuse.

nombre: Improper Session Invalidation after User Logout

consecuencias.nota: When a user changes their credentials, such as a password, they expect that the old password can no longer be used. If an adversary had previously logged in with a password that was compromised, they establish a session that was authenticated with that password and it must be invalidated on password change to prevent future compromise of the account.

descripcion: The product provides a capability for users to change their authentication credentials, such as username or password, but it does not properly invalidate any current authenticated sessions after this authentication credential change.

deteccion.descripcion: Ensure that application testing includes scenarios where user authentication credentials are changed and verify that the previously authenticated sessions can no longer be used.
deteccion.metodo: Dynamic Analysis with Manual Results Interpretation

ejemplos_observados.descripcion: session not invalidated on password change
session not invalidated on password change

mitigaciones.descripcion: Ensure that user sessions are invalidated on the server-side after a change to their authentication credentials. It is important that the server-side handles all session invalidation and does not rely on the client to remove or delete a session due to the possibility of adversaries capturing session identifiers or cookies for later reuse.

nombre: Improper Session Invalidation after Authentication Credential Change

consecuencias.nota: If an authentication artifact is used across multiple applications or services, it allows an adversary who is able to compromise the authentication artifact to gain access to all applications or services that use that artifact.

In order to revoke access to an adversary who has compromised a shared authentication artifact, that artifact must be invalidated which would affect the availability of any user who has legitimately obtained the artifact to authenticate.

descripcion: The product provides an authentication artifact, such as an authentication token, for an authenticated user session, but the same artifact is used for every authenticated user session, potentially across multiple different applications.

mitigaciones.descripcion: Enforce re-authentication per user device. This prevents another user from obtaining the singular authentication artifact and making authenticated requests without authenticating.
Use unique authentication artifacts per user device that will only be accepted if used on that device.
Ensure that unique authentication artifacts are used for each application or service within an organization to prevent potential reuse across applications.

nombre: Use of Singular Authentication Artifact for Multiple User Sessions

consecuencias.nota:
The consequences vary depending on how the credential is
intended for use within the product. If an attacker steals or guesses
the expired credential, then the attacker would have more time than
desired in order to conduct malicious activities.

descripcion: The product receives a request that includes a credential such as a key, certificate, password, confirmation code, or token, but the product does not check whether the credential is expired.

ejemplos_observados.descripcion:
Data-sharing product does not check token properties
including expiry, allowing attackers to bypass the expiration check.

Product does not ensure that a pending invitation is
processed before the specified expiry period.

Chain: product compares an array to a scalar value
(CWE-1024), effectively bypassing an expiry check for a token
(CWE-xxxx).
Product checks expiry for integer values, but not for floats.

introduccion.nota: Developers might check that the credential exists and is known, without checking if it is expired.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
When receiving a credential, look up its expiration to
ensure that the credential is still active. If the incoming credential
states its own expiration, do not trust this value as it may be part
of untrusted input.

Ensure that, for any flow that generates or resets
credentials, the expiration is clearly recorded for the
credential. Also, ensure that mechanisms exist (such as error
handling) for implementations to easily check for expiration, or build
in the expiration check as part of the design.

nombre: Improper Check for Credential Expiration

consecuencias.nota:
If an external identifier is controlled by an attacker, such as
an email address, then the attacker might be able to perform a
"pre-hijacking attack" against a victim who creates or recovers their
account.

descripcion:
The product supports user accounts that include a user's external
identifier or communications channel - such as email, phone number,
social media account, or domain name - but it does not properly verify
that the user actually controls the associated identifier or channel.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
Before changing the contact information, send a message
to the user with a confirmation code. Only make the change when the
user provides the correct code. Ensure that the confirmation code is
expired and rendered invalid if the user does not respond quickly
enough.

nombre: Improper External Identity Verification

consecuencias.nota:
If an input is analyzed and/or processed by multiple components
in security-related situations - such as analyzing headers or
comparing identifiers - then a parser differential could lead to
incorrect security decisions.

descripcion:
The product uses a common specification or format that is shared
between multiple components or entities, but the components have
different parsers that can interpret the same input in different,
security-relevant ways.

deteccion.descripcion:
The different product components or entities could be tested
using inputs with a variety of manipulations, such as differences in
capitalization, whitespace, "boundary" tags, etc. The behavior of each
component could be evaluated to see if the inputs are handled
consistently.

ejemplos_observados.descripcion:
JavaScript-based DOM parser silently accepts certain
malformed end tags such as "</a\nResidue>" due to a parser differential,
possibly preventing the detection of malformed input.

introduccion.nota:
The product's components might be required to follow a
specification that is incomplete in ways that do not sufficiently
cover security expectations, and/or allows for implementation-specific
variations that may be security-critical.

mitigaciones.descripcion: If possible, ensure that the same parser is used by each component.
mitigaciones.efectividad_notas:
This might be difficult to do if the affected
product has some components or entities that are not directly under
its control, such as with firewalls managing traffic between diverse
systems that might have a variety of libraries across different
operating systems, programming languages, etc.

nombre: Insufficiently Controlled Parser Differential

consecuencias.nota:
The consequences vary depending on how the credential is
intended for use within the product. At the least, a long expiration
date gives an attacker more time to steal or guess the credential, and
if compromised, the attacker would have more time than desired in
order to conduct malicious activities.

descripcion:
The product generates or relies on a credential such as a key,
certificate, password, confirmation code, or token, but the credential
does not expire or has an expiration that is too long, i.e., the
expiration is insufficient for the intended security policy of the
product.

deteccion.descripcion:
If the credentials are provided through a communications
protocol, monitor the communications related to credential generation
and examine any expiration dates or times that are set.

Examine the code to determine where credentials are created or
updated, and determine how any expiration dates or times are set.

ejemplos_observados.descripcion:
Video encoder web interface issues authentication tokens
with an expiration time that is longer than the expected session lifetime.

Chain: Learning management system generates tokens
without an expiration (CWE-1472), making its password reset mechanism
weak (CWE-640).

firmware camera system creates an authentication token
with insufficient expiration.

Package manager for Erlang uses password reset tokens
that do not expire.

Wordpress plugin generates a One-Time Password (OTP)
without an expiration (CWE-1472) and does not perform rate-limiting
(CWE-307), allowing attackers to compromise accounts via a brute force
attack.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
For each credential that is created, reset, or used,
ensure that the expiration is set to be as short as possible while
preserving usability.

Design the product to analyze the credentials that it
manages, and provide mechanisms to provide secure defaults, and/or a
capability to warn users about excessive expiration.

nombre: Generation of Credential with Long Expiration

consecuencias.nota:
If the cached data is used for
security-critical functionality such as authentication,
authorization, or identity, then this might allow users
or adversaries to perform operations beyond their
expected lifetime. If the data is old but used for
identification, such as DNS lookup results, then the
stale data could point to entities that are no longer
controlled by the intended owner.

descripcion:
The product uses or supports data in a cache, but it does
not properly specify an expiration with a date, time, or
time period that is sufficient for the intended security
policy of the product or its adminstrators.

ejemplos_observados.descripcion:
RESTful search engine caches DNS hostname lookups
forever in order to prevent DNS spoofing attacks, but
it will not be able to detect when the hostnames
resolve to a different IP address.

introduccion.nota:
Developers might inadvertently omit
specifying a specific expiration for the data. With some
cache mechanisms, this could cause the data to be
labeled as having no expiration at all.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
For each type of cached data, determine the
best lifetime that balances efficiency provided by the
cache with the security implications of the data
becoming too stale. Explicitly specify an expiration
date or time period.

nombre: Improper Expiration of Cached Data

a controlled way. Consider analyzing the data to
extract key elements, such as e-mail addresses or
domain names, to ensure that they are consistent with
the original input.

were correct. These methods could be time-consuming
and not necessarily complete, but there might not be

functionality that the data/state supports.

or function, or it performs a state transition, but it does
not provide some security-critical data/state that is needed
by the receiving component/function.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
Clearly identify security-critical data/state
structures and ensure that they are propagated when
necessary. Be careful of error conditions that could
redirect control flow in a way that prevents the

consecuencias.nota:
The technical impact could include
Memory-access delays, I/O access delays, deadline
miss, etc.
The attacker can leverage this weakness to
generate unbounded delays and denial of service (DoS)
in the access of shared resources. The system
interconnect might be left in an inconsistent state,
requiring a partial or full reset of the network,
according to the implementation. The scenario may
play out as follows. The interconnect receives a write
request from a controller initiator (e.g., sending the
header to the interconnect for writing N words of
data, with N ranging from 1 to the maximum burst
length allowed). The interconnect then speculatively
propagates the request to the target peripheral
through the shared bus before the corresponding data
are received at the interconnect. Here, the word
"speculatively" refers to the fact that the
interconnect propagates the request, assuming that the
controller will at some point provide the data, thus
releasing the use of the bus. This speculatively
reserves the bus to the manager transaction issuer,
which is left free to delay its data provisioning
phase. This reserves the whole bus path between the
initiator and the target peripheral until all of the
words associated with the request are provided by the
controller. If the interconnect assumes a cooperative
behavior from the controller, it is implicitly
trusting that the controller will complete the
transaction and release the bus for use from the other
controllers. A malicious, faulty, or misbehaving
manager module can generate a denial-of-service
condition in preventing access to the write data link
from all of the other managers in the system, and
unboundedly inhibit the write access to one or
multiple peripherals in the system (i.e., memories,
I/Os, etc.).

contexto:
Some products may use an architecture with a
shared bus that is accessible by multiple devices, in
which these devices can issue requests that utilize the
shared bus. There may be an on-chip interconnect based
on a protocol that manages the devices' requests to the
bus and enforces the ordering of requests and data. When
a device makes a request, the bus might indefinitely
lock the write access to a shared output link until the
initiating device finishes its transaction. If the
initiating device does not finish the transaction
quickly enough, this can prevent other devices from
using the bus, causing a denial of service.
A "manager module" is a hardware component that
initiates transactions on the interconnect, such as a
processor, DMA engine, or hardware
accelerator.
descripcion:
The product uses a multi-manager shared bus architecture
with an on-chip interconnect that speculatively propagates
a request for a write transaction, but it does not ensure
that the remaining steps required by the manager module to
complete the request are fulfilled in a timely manner.

deteccion.descripcion:
Instances of this issue can be detected by
manual review of the switching policy implemented in
the interconnect and the deployed on-chip
communication standard.
deteccion.efectividad_notas:
Manual review requires to have a full
description of the architecture of the
interconnect. This information might not be available
when a third-party interconnect is used.

deteccion.descripcion:
Instances of this issue can be found in
manager modules by using property-based verification
specifically targeting the detection of stalls
propagated to the shared resources
[REF-1588].

Instances of this issue can be found in
simulation by synthetically generating stalls at the
input of the interconnect and evaluating if the
interconnect propagates the stalls at the output or
not.
deteccion.efectividad_notas:
Simulations should be capable of triggering
the stalls. Not all of the Verification IP for on-chip
communications might be capable of triggering this
issue.

ejemplos_observados.descripcion:
Certain commercial AXI interconnect IPs
could allow a manager to cause bus stalls.

introduccion.nota:
This occurs if the on-chip communication
interconnect is based on a multi-channel on-chip
communication standard assuming cooperative behavior
among the manager modules AND an unsafe switching
methodology (e.g., cut-through) is in use. Some
switching methodologies may be susceptible to this
weakness in modern on-chip multi-channel communication
standards, such as the cut-through switching policy, a
switching methodology for high performance commonly
implemented at the interconnect level. In cut-through,
a request is propagated independently on the receipt
at the interconnect level of the corresponding
data. If the manager module issuing a write request
delays the provisioning of the corresponding data, the
other manager modules experience delays in accessing
the bus. Such delays are capable of generating denial
of service.

mitigaciones.descripcion:
SoC architects can use a switching
methodology stopping stalls from being propagated to
the interconnect, such as Cut-and-Forward
[REF-1585][REF-1587] or
Store-and-Forward. Alternatively, a monitoring and
recovery module can be added between the interconnect
and each manager module to detect stalls introduced by
the module and restore a safe state in the
interconnect after a stall has been detected
[REF-1586].
mitigaciones.efectividad_notas:
The architect should evaluate which
methodology better suits the target platform, trading
off performance and resource consumption impact
[REF-1585][REF-1586][REF-1587].

nombre: Improper Request Propagation before Data Reception in Write Transactions in a Bus Architecture
